children: “Godzilla Minus Zero” topped the domestic box office with an estimated $31.61 million in its opening weekend, leading four new releases among the five highest-grossing films, according to Rentrak’s studio-reported estimates for Nov. 6-8.
The top 10 films generated a combined $105.68 million. Domestic box office covers the United States and Canada only, excluding ticket sales from other international markets.

For investors in movie studios and theater operators, the results offer a snapshot of audience demand as the holiday movie season approaches. New releases supplied much of the weekend’s revenue, while several returning titles posted relatively modest declines. Ticket sales alone, however, don’t establish profitability, which also depends on production costs, marketing spending and the division of revenue with theaters.

Distributed by GKIDS, “Godzilla Minus Zero” played in 3,254 locations and earned an average of $9,714 per location, the highest average among the top 10. Its estimated Friday gross of $14.6 million accounted for nearly half its weekend total.
“The Cat in the Hat” opened in second place with $20.5 million across 4,003 locations, the widest release on the chart. Angel’s “Drummer Boy” debuted in third with $9.31 million from 2,850 locations.

A24’s “You Can See Everything” placed fourth with $8.86 million in its fourth weekend, down 23% despite losing 770 locations. Its cumulative domestic gross reached $79.8 million, the largest total among the weekend’s top 10.

“Ramayana,” listed under distributor SPRI, opened in fifth place with $8.65 million at 1,433 locations. Its $6,036 average per location ranked second among the top 10, and its reported cumulative domestic earnings stood at $12.16 million.
“Wildwood” collected $7 million in its third weekend, down 22%, bringing its domestic total to $39.82 million. Warner Bros.’
“Clayface” followed with $6.68 million, declining 39% in its third weekend for a cumulative $56.61 million.

New releases “Wild Horse Nine” and “Stray Kids World Tour ‘RUN’ LIVE VIEWING” earned $6 million and $3.72 million, respectively. “Wicker” rounded out the chart with $3.35 million in its third weekend, down 23%, lifting its domestic total to $19.89 million.

Source: Rentrak studio-reported estimates. All figures are estimates through Sunday, Nov. 8.
